name: Toolformer (Self-Supervised Tool-Use Training)
executive_summary: Train the model itself, in a self-supervised way from just a handful of demonstrations per API, to decide which tool to call, when to call it, what arguments to pass, and how to weave the result back into generation.
description: Distinct from ReAct: rather than a prompting pattern applied to an off-the-shelf model, Toolformer trains the model to autonomously insert API calls (calculator, Q&A system, search engines, translation, calendar) into its own generation wherever doing so would have reduced the model's loss on the next tokens, using self-generated candidate API calls filtered by whether they actually help. The result is a model that spontaneously decides for itself when a tool call would help, without a hand-written ReAct-style Thought/Action/Observation scaffold in the prompt. Reports substantially improved zero-shot performance across downstream tasks, often competitive with much larger models, without sacrificing core language modeling ability.
when_to_use: You control fine-tuning and want tool-use behavior built into the model's own generation policy, rather than depending on the prompt to scaffold every tool interaction explicitly.
when_not_to_use: Working with a fixed, already-trained model with no fine-tuning access — use ReAct's pure-prompting approach instead.
known_pitfalls: Requires self-supervised training infrastructure and the specific set of tools the model is trained on; doesn't generalize to a novel tool at inference time the way a well-designed ReAct prompt can, since tool-selection behavior is baked in at training time.

primary_source.authors: Schick, Dwivedi-Yu, Dessì, Raileanu, Lomeli, Zettlemoyer, Cancedda, Scialom
primary_source.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools

variables.name: text_prefix
variables.description: The text preceding a candidate insertion point

variables.name: candidate_api_call
variables.description: A self-generated candidate API call (tool name + arguments)

variables.name: ground_truth_continuation
variables.description: The actual next tokens used to score whether the call helped

variables.name: api_call_result
variables.description: What the tool returned for the candidate call

variables.name: loss_reduction_threshold
variables.description: Minimum loss reduction required to keep a candidate as a training example

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: This template describes a training-time process (fine-tuning or policy training), not a single reproducible inference call; reproducibility depends on the training pipeline and data, not on prompt text alone.
